sheet-1-1.description: The main map of sheet 1 covers the centre of Carneys Point village, the company town built by E. I. du Pont de Nemours & Co. beside its powder works, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Shell Road crosses the sheet diagonally from the lower left to the upper right and is the spine of the area. North-west of it lies a regular grid of small blocks between Kron and Kent, crossed by 1st to 5th Streets and by Broadway, and east of Kent the lettered streets A to D run to Walker Avenue. Between Shell Road and Kent are Eden Street, Delaware Avenue and a short stretch of Broadway. South-east of Shell Road the streets Schley, Astrid, Mix, Thelma, Peley and Birch Street and the I and H Avenues form a second, later block pattern of uniform dwelling lots. Almost every building is a one- or two-storey frame dwelling, numbered with house numbers in the 2000s, with a few stores, a post office and a steam laundry along Shell Road and Delaware Avenue. A fire department house, hose carts and fire alarm boxes are marked, and the Community Church and a public school stand near Kent and A Street. A pumping station and a fire supply reservoir stand at the west edge, where a margin note refers to the powder mills of the du Pont company beyond. The sheet also carries the title cartouche, the key, the specials index and a small location map of New Jersey, all left out of this part, and a boxed inset of the Kent to Walker Avenue blocks, which is part 2.
notes: Kent is now Division Street; Kron is now Cleveland Avenue.

The numbered streets west of Kent now carry other names: 5th Street is E Street, 4th Street is C Street, 3rd Street is B Street, 2nd Street and Eden Street are Johnson Street, 1st Street is Garfield Street (identified from the fit).
Schley is now Market Street, Astrid is Laurel Street, Mix is Oak Street, H Avenue is Jackson Street and I Avenue is Ives Avenue.
East of Kent the drawn letter streets do not line up exactly with today's A to E Streets; residuals of 3 to 6 m remain across the part.
Margin note: powder mills of the E. I. du Pont de Nemours Co. beyond the west edge.

map, 100 ft to an inch. Carneys Point village around Shell Road (Broadway, Kent, Walker, numbered and lettered streets) with title cartouche, key, index and NJ location map. Three parts: 1 main map (north about 42 deg clockwise from up); 2 boxed inset at right, Kent Avenue to Walker Avenue between J and D Streets, drawn square to the page (north about 63 deg); 3 lower-right grid, Schley Avenue to Ada between F and B Avenues, which does not fit one transformation with part 1 (fitted separately, same scale). Main map drawn on a slightly different footing from modern streets: RMSE 3.5 m.

sheet-1-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 1 is a boxed inset at the right edge of the sheet, framed by a heavy line, that continues the lettered streets of Carneys Point north-west along Kent and Walker Avenue. It is drawn square to the page, with Kent on the left and Walker Avenue on the right, so north lies about 63 degrees clockwise from the top, unlike the main map. From top to bottom it shows J, I, H, G, F, E and D Streets. The upper blocks, numbered 25 to 28, are uniform rows of one-storey frame dwellings on narrow lots with rear alleys. The lower blocks, 29 and 32, hold the community buildings of the company town: a Y.M.C.A. building with a library and gymnasium, a movie hall, a print shop, an office and a carpenter shop, with a fire alarm box on Walker Avenue. Water pipes are marked in the streets and fire hydrants at the corners. The inset repeats part of the ground drawn on sheet 2, which shows the east side of Walker Avenue between the same streets.
notes: Kent is now Division Street.

The drawn spacing of F, E and D Streets is longer than today's: F Street is drawn about 60 ft further from G Street than the modern junctions; the F Street junctions were left out of the fit and the lower half of the inset rests on J to G Street.
Y.M.C.A. building with library, gymnasium and movies.

sheet-1-3.description: Part 3 of sheet 1 is the lower right corner of the sheet: a regular grid of company dwellings south-east of the Carneys Point village centre, between Schley Avenue at the top and Ada at the bottom, crossed by F, E, D, C and B Avenues. It includes block 210 on Peley north of Schley Avenue and parts of blocks 217 and 221 at the edges. Every block is divided into equal lots with one- or two-storey frame dwellings, house numbers in the 2000s, and a few small sheds; a pump house stands at the corner of C Avenue and Schley Avenue, and a fire alarm box at D Avenue and Astrid. Water pipes, marked arbitrary house numbering and street widths of 40 ft are noted. The area is drawn at the same 100 ft scale as the rest of the sheet but does not fit one transformation with the main map, so it was placed as a separate part.
notes: Schley Avenue is now Market Street, Astrid is Laurel Street, Ada is Holly Street.
F Avenue is now Green Street, E Avenue Wilson Avenue, D Avenue Taft Avenue, C Avenue Polk Avenue; Peley appears to be Center Street.
B Avenue was not matched; modern Georgetown Road runs through the blocks between C and B Avenues.

sheet-2-1.description: The main map of sheet 2 continues Carneys Point east of sheet 1, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north about 63 degrees clockwise from the top. Its left half is the grid of lettered streets, J to B Street, between Walker Avenue and Bay, with blocks 49 to 89 of uniform one-storey frame dwellings and rear alleys. East of Bay lie Magnolia Street, Ash Street and Poplar Street with large vacant blocks numbered 63 to 87, the Wesleyan Methodist Church, a fire department house on G Street, and an athletic field between Boulevard and Cypress, with a short row of dwellings on Pine, Cypress and Elk at the top. Shell Road crosses diagonally from the lower left to the upper right, with the first M.E. Church, a garage, and stores. South of it are the Lafayette public school (brick), a public school and annex, a second public school by Walker Avenue, and blocks around Springfield, Strand Street, Harrison, Grant Street, Lincoln Avenue, Madison Street, Jefferson, Adams Street, Washington Street, Carlisle Avenue, Lehigh Avenue and Georgetown Road, mostly vacant. Fire alarm boxes and hydrants are marked throughout. Two parts of the sheet framed by heavy lines are drawn separately: the inset at middle right (part 2, not placed) and the Penns Grove border area at lower right (part 3).
notes: Bay is now Bay Street; Boulevard appears to be East Hoover Street.
The blocks south of Shell Road (Lincoln Avenue, Carlisle Avenue, Lehigh Avenue, Adams Street, Washington Street) have no matching modern streets.
Walker Avenue junctions are hand-picked: the detector paired alley and lot lines there.
Lafayette public school, brick.

map, 100 ft to an inch. Walker Avenue to Bay Street, J to A Streets, Shell Road, Lafayette public school, athletic field; north about 63 deg. Three parts separated by heavy lines: 1 main map; 2 inset middle right (Georgetown Road, 11th to 13th Streets, 1st and 2nd Avenues), not placed; 3 inset lower right (Clyde, Garnet, Spring, Summerill, Church, E. Maple, Bera, J Street; 'These risks also shown on 1921 map of Penns Grove'), drawn turned to fit the page, placed from five junctions.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Georgetown Road, 11th, 12th and 13th Streets, 1st and 2nd Avenues (blocks 224 to 229) (no matching modern street junction found; the development appears to have been cleared; needs identification of the area on the ground).

sheet-2-3.description: Part 3 of sheet 2 is the inset at the lower right of the sheet, framed by heavy lines, showing the edge of Penns Grove adjoining Carneys Point; a note says these risks are also shown on the 1921 map of Penns Grove. It is drawn turned to fit the page. Clyde Street and Garnet run along the left, Spring Avenue and Summerill Avenue cross the middle, Church runs to East Maple Avenue, and the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad branch line to the powder plants of E. I. du Pont de Nemours & Co. crosses the lower part. South of the railroad are Bera and J Street between Boulevard, Pine Street, Cypress and Elk Street, with Shell Road at the right. Most buildings are one- and two-storey frame dwellings; a fire department house stands on Spring Avenue, the brick Episcopal Church of Our Blessed Saviour with its chapel stands south of the railroad, and a fireproof transformer house is drawn at the right edge.
notes: Church is now part of Garnet Street; the south end of the drawn Shell Road is on the line of today's East Maple Avenue; J Street appears to be Hayes Street.
The railroad branch to the du Pont powder plants is shown; part of its line is now Plant Road.
Placed from five junctions only (RMSE 1.3 m, leave-one-out 6.5 m); low confidence away from Garnet Street.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 shows Deep Water Village and Dupont City, located two miles south of Carneys Point beside the Salem Canal, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north about 63 degrees clockwise from the top. Salem Avenue crosses the sheet from a draw bridge over the canal at the left. North of it is Deep Water Village, a company settlement of small frame dwellings on Juno, Joel, Reller and Essex Street, crossed by Salem Road, Camph, Butte and Nueche, with a public school, the Deep Water Methodist Church, a fire department house, a water tower and a transformer yard; a note describes the village water system owned by the du Pont company. South of Salem Avenue is Dupont City, a planned grid of long narrow lots on Penns Avenue, Arlington Avenue and Hopewell Avenue, crossed by Broadway, Main, Chester, Plant, Clark, Highland and Norwood. Only a scattering of dwellings has been built there; stores, a public school and the Dupont City Nazarene Church face Salem Avenue. Most blocks are lettered A to T and many lots are empty.
notes: Salem Avenue is now North Broadway; Highland is now Pine Street; Broadway is Broadway Street.

The Deep Water Village streets north of Salem Avenue (Juno, Joel, Reller, Essex Street, Salem Road, Camph, Butte, Nueche) did not match today's streets there consistently and were left out of the fit; the placement rests on Salem Avenue and the Dupont City grid.
Draw bridge over the canal at Salem Avenue.

map, 100 ft to an inch. Deep Water Village and Dupont City, 'located 2 miles S. of Carneys Point' (Deepwater, Pennsville Township), along the Salem Canal; north about 63 deg. One part. Placed from Salem Avenue (now North Broadway) and the Dupont City grid (Penns, Chester, Plant, Clark, Highland, Norwood); the Deep Water Village streets north of Salem Avenue (Juno, Joel, Reller, Essex) do not match the modern streets there and were left out of the fit.
